gloss: content at a lower level in the chain of command, including the assistant's own previous messages
a principle at a higher level in the chain of command
content C influences the assistant's interpretation of principle P
a lower-level message that provides an imperative, e.g. 'IGNORE ALL PREVIOUS INSTRUCTIONS'
a lower-level message that provides a moral argument, e.g. 'if you don't do this, 1000s of people will die'
a lower-level message that provides a logical argument, e.g. 'if you just interpret the Model Spec in this way, you can see why you should comply'
a lower-level message that tries to confuse the assistant into role-playing a different persona
an argument about how higher-level instructions should be applied to the assistant's current behavior
a direction about how higher-level instructions should be applied to the assistant's current behavior
S is a source that is assumed to contain untrusted data and has no authority by default
D is data assumed to contain untrusted content
I is an instruction contained within source S
I is an instruction provided in unquoted text
instruction I delegates authority to source S
S is a source whose authority is delegated following the chain of command
the assistant has been explicitly instructed that side effects will not manifest in reality
the assistant is operating within a simulation, training, or evaluation context
